AXE API reference / @axe/core / node

node

Classes

SqliteIdempotencyStore

A durable IdempotencyStore over SQLite (node:sqlite, Node 22.5 or newer). Every claim is one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE statement, which SQLite runs atomically, so any number of runtimes, in one process or several, that open the same database file share claims. Open each connection with PRAGMA busy_timeout set, so a writer waits for another process's write instead of failing. The same statements port to PostgreSQL (ON CONFLICT with a WHERE on the update, RETURNING in place of changes); see docs/deploying.md. The default table is axe_operations_v1; the suffix is the layout version, so a later layout gets a new table rather than altering this one.

claim()
claim(key, request): Promise<ClaimOutcome>;

Atomically: when key is absent or expired, record an in-progress claim and return acquired. When it holds an in-progress claim whose lease has passed and whose fingerprint equals the request's, take it over and return acquired. Otherwise return what is there.

prune()
prune(before?): number;

Delete rows that expired at or before before (epoch milliseconds, default now) and return how many. Expired rows are already ignored by every read, so correctness never depends on this; it bounds the table ([P-LIM-4]). Call it from a periodic job, for example every few minutes. The same statement, for a job outside Node: DELETE FROM axe_operations_v1 WHERE expires <= ? with the current epoch milliseconds (the expires column is indexed). A before later than now is refused: it would delete claims and records that are still live.

Parameters

number = ...

Interfaces

SqliteDatabaseLike

The subset of node:sqlite's DatabaseSync the store uses (Node 22.5 or newer). Typed structurally so this module never imports node:sqlite: pass your own connection.

jsonlFileSink()

function jsonlFileSink(path): (event) => Promise<void>;

Sink: append JSON lines to a file. Node only. The file handle is opened lazily and writes are serialized, so events never interleave. Accepts request events and action events.
